goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 offers passkey authentication to any identified user without verifying they have a passwordless WebAuthn credential, producing an unusable re-authentication option

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. Looking at UsernamePasswordForm.java:160, the method `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` at line 160-162 checks `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. This enables passkey UI when passkeys feature is enabled for the realm and user is identified. The passkey conditional UI is designed to work with discoverable credentials that don't require pre-checking user credentials - the browser/authenticator handles credential discovery. The tests in the diff (like `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`) show this working correctly. The finding incorrectly assumes the code should verify WebAuthn credentials exist before showing the passkey option, but conditional UI passkeys work differently - they allow the authenticator to discover available credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:64 returns false from shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators for a known re-authentication user, omitting the credential allow-list and allowing unrelated local accounts that Keycloak rejects

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that returning false from shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators causes a security issue by 'allowing unrelated local accounts that Keycloak rejects'. However, examining the diff shows this method controls whether WebAuthn authenticators are displayed in the UI during conditional passkeys login flow. The method returning false simply means the authenticator list won't be shown on screen - it doesn't affect the actual authentication validation. The WebAuthn authentication still happens via the conditional UI mechanism (autocomplete='webauthn'), and credential validation occurs server-side. The tests in the diff (webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication, webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication) demonstrate that passkeys authentication works correctly during re-authentication. The finding misunderstands the purpose of this method.
